confirmed_blocking.summary: ENG-26 / FR-003: on the documented first-fix flow, checkpoint review --next fix --design-fix silently skips the reservation but still moves the stage to fix.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: The reservation is written only when the stored stage is already 'review' (line 930). SKILL.md step 7 has no checkpoint into review before the first verdict. This run went implement (3e81adc, after verify-pass) straight to fix through the first checkpoint review --next fix. With --design-fix on that flow, line 930 is false, no pending_design_fix is stored, and target 'fix' is still written. The command exits 0, so the orchestrator believes the reservation exists. FR-003 says the flag 'creates a reservation', and design-code-mapping.md:102 says it 'atomically sets stage: fix and review.pending_design_fix'. The only test (test_commands.py:862) starts from stage review. The retry-idempotence intent is served just as well by skipping only when the stored stage is already 'fix'.
confirmed_blocking.fix: Write the reservation whenever the stored stage is not already 'fix' (or on any legitimate transition into fix from review/implement/verify), and keep the retry no-op once the stage is fix. Add a CLI test that starts at stage implement with a recorded verify-pass and a round-1 verdict, runs checkpoint review --next fix --design-fix, and asserts the reservation {attempt: fix_rounds+1, round, verdict}. Also assert that a retry does not rewrite it.
